cohort: The study included 56 parturients scheduled for elective caesarean sections under spinal anaesthesia.
finding: Intrathecal morphine provides superior analgesia and reduces the need for rescue analgesia compared to clonidine in post-caesarean patients, with manageable side effects and no adverse effects on neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Intrathecal morphine offers superior analgesia and reduced rescue analgesia requirements for patients undergoing caesarean sections compared to clonidine, without adverse neonatal effects.
followup_time: at least 13.8 hours post-surgery (for duration of analgesia)
